title: Continuation Fixed-Point Semantics

basis.scope: Introduce bounded fixed-point semantics for continuation expressions. This patch defines the mathematical meaning of fixed points within the RT Calculus without asserting existence, uniqueness, admissibility, or correctness for all continuation classes.

core_rule.statement: Continuation fixed-point semantics apply only after EVAL_024 and only to continuation expressions typed in ClassFix with a declared Φ(C); bounded EvalΦ(C) may yield Fix(C) within the declared evaluation regime; recursive and higher-order continuations may generate candidates where admissible; REDUCE_025 remains governing; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Introduce bounded fixed-point semantics for continuation expressions. This patch defines the mathematical meaning of fixed points within the RT Calculus without asserting existence, uniqueness, admissibility, or correctness for all continuation classes.

canonical_claims.statement: Fixed-point semantics are bounded and apply only to typed continuation expressions in ClassFix.
Φ(C) is declared and EvalΦ(C) is bounded without asserting universal existence or uniqueness.
Recursive and higher-order continuations may generate fixed-point candidates where admissible.
Deferred fixed-point evaluation remains governed by REDUCE_025 and the existing outcome taxonomy.

formal_objects.name: Continuation Fixed Point
formal_objects.definition: A continuation expression whose fixed-point evaluation under Φ reaches a continuation condition invariant under further applications of Φ within the declared bounded evaluation regime.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Operator
formal_objects.definition: A declared operator over continuation expressions used to evaluate whether repeated application reaches an invariant continuation condition.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Evaluation
formal_objects.definition: The bounded evaluation process of a continuation expression C under the declared fixed-point operator Φ.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Candidate
formal_objects.definition: A continuation expression C for which Φ(C) is well-formed and boundedly evaluable as a possible fixed-point witness.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Class
formal_objects.definition: The typed class of continuation expressions eligible for bounded fixed-point semantic interpretation.

fixed_point_pipeline.operation: Verify well-formedness, typing, and ClassFix eligibility.
Continue reduction using REDUCE_025 where appropriate.

fixed_point_classes.description: Continuation satisfies bounded fixed-point semantics and yields Fix(C) under EvalΦ(C).
Continuation remains under evaluation as a fixed-point candidate.
Fixed-point semantics cannot yet be established within the current calculus boundary.
Evaluation terminates in classified continuation failure.

semantic_rule.statement: C may receive fixed-point semantics only when C is typed in ClassFix, Φ(C) is declared, EvalΦ(C) is bounded, and EvalΦ(C) yields an invariant continuation condition Fix(C).

non_claims: Does not assert that every continuation has a fixed point.

relationships.higher_order_continuation: HC(C) may operate on fixed-point candidates.
relationships.fixed_point_evaluation: EvalΦ(C) is the bounded evaluation process for candidate fixed points.
relationships.reduction: REDUCE_025 remains the governing reduction procedure.
relationships.partial_normal_form: Deferred fixed-point evaluation may terminate as pNF(C).

invariants: EvalΦ(C) is bounded and diagnostic only.
Fixed-point semantics do not imply existence.
Fixed-point semantics do not imply uniqueness.
Fixed-point semantics do not imply admissibility.
